concept_definition: Relating to, derived from, or characteristic of living organisms.
Relating to the nucleus of a cell.
No longer existing because all members of a species or group have died.
Active mainly or exclusively at night, especially of an animal or plant.
Relating to, involving, or consisting of muscles.
Preserved as or relating to a fossil.
Relating to the production of offspring or to the biological processes and organs involved in producing offspring.
Capable of reproducing or producing offspring.
Living in or occurring in the sea or ocean.
Producing flowers; in bloom.
Relating to genes, heredity, or the transmission of characteristics from parents to offspring.
Brought into existence by birth; having been born.
Made in a factory or by an industrial process rather than occurring naturally.
In grammar, belonging to a gender category traditionally associated with male beings, or having a form used for that category.
Relating to a person's physical constitution or general bodily makeup.
Relating to the evolutionary history and relationships of organisms or other biological groups.
Relating to, situated in, or forming the spine or spinal column.
Relating to the spinal cord.
Relating to, containing, or consisting of vessels that carry fluids, especially blood vessels in the body or conducting tissues in plants.
Derived from a single common ancestral group and including all of its descendants; describing a taxonomic group that forms a complete clade.
Relating to a taxonomic group that includes a common ancestor and some, but not all, of its descendants.
Living in or on another organism and obtaining food or other benefits from it, usually while harming the host.
Relating to, caused by, or characteristic of a fungus or fungi.
Containing or consisting of substantial soft flesh or pulp, especially a plant part or fruit.
Of a plant, living for more than two years and typically flowering repeatedly.
Having a backbone or spinal column; belonging to the group of animals with backbones.
Feeding mainly or exclusively on animals or animal flesh.
Relating specifically to the bony pelvis or its anatomical structures, especially in medical or anatomical terminology.
Relating to the thyroid gland or its hormones.
Relating to, forming, or resembling a skeleton or the bones that support a body.
Relating to, resembling, or characteristic of a larva or the larval stage of an animal.
Having or showing toes of a specified kind or number.
Having fins or fin-like structures.
Relating to the brain, especially the cerebrum.
Feeding mainly or exclusively on plants.
Relating to, forming, or belonging to a vertebra or the vertebral column (spine).
Relating to urine or the organs and processes involved in producing and excreting urine.
Relating to the movement of blood through the heart and blood vessels, or to the body's circulatory system.
Unable to fly, especially because of lacking the physical ability to fly; used chiefly of birds and some insects.
Having the characteristics of a herb; nonwoody, with a soft stem that usually dies back after the growing season.
Relating to nutrition, especially the nourishment and health effects provided by food.
Relating to, consisting of, or characteristic of epithelium, the tissue that covers body surfaces, lines internal cavities, and forms many glands.
Relating to, belonging to, or involving the placenta.
Involving or characterized by a close, usually mutually beneficial relationship between different organisms.
Relating to plants or the scientific study of plants.
Describing a person whose gender identity differs from the sex they were assigned at birth.
Relating to the science of the motion, behavior, and effects of projectiles, especially bullets, shells, and missiles.
Not consisting of or derived from living matter; relating to substances that are not produced by living organisms, especially in chemistry.
Relating specifically to the refraction of light by the eye or to the optical power of the eye and its corrective lenses.
Involving, relating to, or occurring between people of the same sex.
Involving sexual or romantic relationships between people of the same sex.
Not human; relating to or characteristic of an animal, machine, artificial intelligence, or other entity that is not a person.
Including or involving people from two or more different ethnic groups.
Using the left hand more skillfully or habitually than the right hand.
Having received a good, broad, or advanced education.
Consisting of or having only one cell, especially referring to an organism whose entire body is made up of a single cell.
Living independently in the natural environment rather than as a parasite, symbiont, or organism maintained by humans.
Designating a species or type of animal whose tail is white or has a distinctive white underside or tip.
Consisting entirely of females or women; involving only female members or participants.
Having a body temperature that varies with the surrounding environment; ectothermic.
Having learned a subject or skill independently, without formal instruction from a teacher or educational institution.
Producing and depositing eggs, especially as a way of reproducing.
Able to speak or use two languages.
Relating to or characteristic of birds.
Having ears or ear-like parts, especially of a specified kind or number.
Existing in a person or thing from birth or from the beginning, rather than acquired through experience or learning.
Produced by forcing air through a narrow passage so that friction is created; relating to fricative consonants or their articulation.
Produced by completely blocking and then suddenly releasing the airflow in the vocal tract.
Produced with a hissing sound, especially describing a speech sound made by directing air through a narrow passage in the mouth.
Relating to or produced by the glottis, the opening between the vocal folds.
Produced by placing the tongue against or near the hard palate, as in certain speech sounds.
Relating to or produced with the back part of the tongue raised against or near the soft palate.
Produced with the lips, especially a speech sound articulated by bringing the lips together or toward the teeth.
Relating to or characterized by the pronunciation of the sound /r/, especially the pronunciation of /r/ after a vowel, as in American English and many varieties of Scottish English.
Of or relating to speech sounds produced with relatively unobstructed airflow and prominent resonance.
Relating to the sounds of human speech, especially their production, transmission, or perception.
Relating to phonemes or to the way speech sounds function as contrastive units in a particular language.
Having a white tail or a tail with a conspicuous white section; used especially to describe animals.
Relating to taxonomy, especially the classification and naming of organisms.
Relating to sex, sexual activity, or the physical aspects of reproduction.
Relating to the distinction between male and female sexes or to an organism's sex.
Able to spread an infectious illness from one person to another.
Having seeds or containing seeds.
Sown or planted with seeds.
By means of fertilization of an egg with sperm outside the body, as part of assisted reproduction.
At risk of harm, loss, or destruction; threatened with extinction, especially when referring to a species.
Living forever or incapable of dying; not subject to death.
Not wild or fearful of people; accustomed to living with or being handled by humans.
Growing or developing strongly and rapidly; healthy and robust.
Living, growing, or found in or near water.
Lacking sexual organs or sexual reproduction; reproducing without the fusion of gametes.
Relating to, caused by, or consisting of bacteria.
Relating to or consisting of capillaries, or to capillary action.
Relating to the heart, especially its structure or function.
Relating to the process of growth, change, or progress over time, especially in a person, organism, or system.
Relating specifically to the physical, cognitive, or emotional development of a person, especially a child.
Relating to digestion or the process by which food is broken down and absorbed by the body.
Having two complete sets of chromosomes, one inherited from each parent; describing a cell or organism with this chromosome complement.
Relating to or characteristic of an embryo, especially during its earliest stage of development.
Relating to glands or cells that release hormones directly into the blood, or to the hormones and processes associated with them.
Relating to evolution, especially the gradual development or change of living things, ideas, or systems over time.
Relating to a fetus or characteristic of a fetus, especially during development in the uterus.
Living, occurring, or designed for use in water that is not salty.
Relating to the external reproductive organs, or to the reproductive organs generally.
Having a single set of unpaired chromosomes in each cell, as in the gametes of many organisms.

Having the same or a corresponding position, structure, or function because of a shared origin or relationship; especially, referring to structures in different organisms that derive from the same ancestral structure.
Protected from a particular disease or infection, especially because of vaccination or previous exposure.
Invading or spreading into a place, area, or organism, especially where it is not wanted or is harmful.
Relating to young people who are not yet legally adults, or intended for them.
Of, relating to, or characteristic of mammals, a class of warm-blooded vertebrate animals that feed their young with milk.
Moving from one region or place to another at regular times, especially seasonally, as part of a recurring pattern.
Relating to mitochondria, the structures in cells that produce much of the energy the cell uses.
Relating to nerves or the nervous system, especially in the body.
Relating to photosynthesis or involving the process by which an organism uses light energy to make chemical energy from carbon dioxide and water.
Relating to the normal functions and processes of a living organism or one of its parts.
Caused by, arising from, or characteristic of the normal bodily processes of a living organism, rather than being psychological or pathological.
Relating to the pituitary gland, a small gland at the base of the brain that produces hormones.
Relating to an animal that hunts, kills, and eats other animals.
Relating to the lungs.
Of an action, response, or movement: occurring automatically and without conscious thought.
Relating to breathing or to the process by which an organism takes in oxygen and releases carbon dioxide.
Relating to the organs and structures involved in breathing, especially as a field of medical care or study.
Relating to or affecting the body as a whole, rather than being limited to one organ or area.
Relating to the vagina or involving the vagina.
Caused by, relating to, or involving a virus, especially a disease or infection.
Having wings; equipped with or possessing wings.
Subject to death; not living forever.
Causing or capable of causing death; fatal.
Relating to or characteristic of an epidemic; occurring in a widespread and rapidly increasing way.
Producing flowers or covered with flowers.
Relating to the nervous system, especially the brain, spinal cord, and nerves, or to the medical study and treatment of disorders affecting them.
Dangerous and likely to attack or cause harm, especially of an animal.
In genetics, describing an allele or trait that is expressed in an organism even when only one copy of the relevant allele is present.
Regularly found among or characteristic of a particular people, place, or region; native to and restricted to a specific geographic area, especially of a plant or animal.
Relating to short, intense physical activity that relies primarily on energy sources other than oxygen-dependent aerobic metabolism.
Relating to the heart and the blood vessels, especially as a body system or in matters of health and disease.
Relating to the cells of living organisms, especially biological cells.
Relating to eukaryotes or characteristic of them; describing organisms or cells whose cells have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
Relating to, formed by, or characteristic of glaciers or the geological period when glaciers were widespread.
Relating to metabolism, the chemical processes by which living organisms convert food and other substances into energy and the materials needed for growth and maintenance.
Relating to or caused by microbes, especially microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and viruses.
Consisting of or made up of many cells; having more than one cell, especially of an organism.
Living or growing on land rather than in water; of or relating to land-dwelling organisms.
Relating to the relationships between living things and their environment, or to the scientific study of those relationships.
Capable of living, growing, or developing; especially, able to survive outside the womb or laboratory conditions.
Causing or resulting in death.
Relating to biology, living organisms, or the processes and characteristics of life.
Related by direct genetic descent or parentage, rather than by adoption or another social or legal relationship.
Relating to movement or the muscles and nerves that produce movement.
Unable to produce or support plant growth; having soil that is poor, dry, or otherwise unproductive.
Not producing offspring; unable to conceive or reproduce.
Passed from parents to their children through genes or biological inheritance.
Able to be transmitted from one person, animal, or organism to another and cause disease.
Occurring or functioning automatically, without conscious control, especially in reference to bodily processes or muscles.
Relating to, intended for, or characteristic of infants.
Basic and innate, rather than learned or controlled by reasoning; instinctive.
Relating to or resembling an alveolus, especially one of the tiny air sacs in the lungs.
Relating to the teeth or to dentistry.
Relating to the form, structure, or development of an organism or its parts, especially as studied in biology.
